details:
**Ulysses** – contains the famous line “To strive, to seek, to find, and not to yield.”  
**The Charge of the Light Brigade** – features the refrain “Half a league onward, all in the valley of death, rode the six hundred.”  
**In Memoriam A.H.H.** – includes the lament “‘Tis better to have loved and lost than never to have loved at all.”  
**Crossing the Bar** – concludes with the plea “I hope to see my Pilot face to face.”  
**The Lady of Shalott** – notes the mirror’s crack and the doomed isolation of the titular lady.  
**Break, Break, Break** – a mournful elegy for A.H.H., lamenting the loss of a beloved.  
**The Lotos-Eaters** – recounts a Greek myth about men who abandon their duties in a dreamlike state.  
**The Kraken** – depicts a vast, ancient sea monster terrorizing the deep.  
**Tithonus** – tells the story of a man cursed with eternal life but never aging.  
**Sunset and Evening Star** – opens with the line “Sunset and evening star, and one clear call for me!” describing longing.  
**Half a league onward** – repeated motif in *The Charge of the Light Brigade*, underscoring the relentless march of the soldiers.  
**I hope to see my Pilot face to face** – recurring yearning in several of Tennyson’s poems, symbolizing the desire to confront death.
